players.product: hyperscale rack-level AC-DC power shelves / server power supplies and modular 800 V DC-DC & AC-DC data-center power products

quarterly_data.signal: Q1 results (CFO Paul Oldham): revenue of $511 million increased 26% year-over-year, ahead of guidance and driven by strong data center computing revenue; gross margin 40.1%, achieving the initial milestone of gross margin over 40% and the highest level since the Artesyn acquisition in 2019; record operating income of $98 million with operating margin 19.1%; EPS $2.09, up 70% year-over-year. Telecom and networking revenue rose to $25 million on AI-related networking programs.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $511 million (+26% YoY); gross margin 40.1%; operating income $98 million; operating margin 19.1%; EPS $2.09 (+70% YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: Data center computing revenue was another record, up 9% sequentially and 102% year-over-year. Oldham: 'we continue to experience frequent customer changes in demand mix due to various downstream constraints'; that volatility is expected to limit revenue in Q2 ('data center will moderate sequentially based on timing of customer deliveries'), with the ramp of several programs supporting a stronger second half. CEO Steve Kelley said the Q1 beat was not a pull-in but came as customers addressed downstream supply constraints, and that 'there's definitely a bias to the upside in our 2026 forecast'.
quarterly_data.figure: data center computing revenue $194 million (+9% sequentially, +102% YoY)

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 data center revenue growth outlook raised to the mid-30s on 'strong customer adoption of our high-power AI solutions', with sequential growth expected in the second half. Oldham: 'We don't have any forecast for our second wave customers in our guidance for 2026. Any of that we're able to pull in would be upside to the 35% growth.'
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 data center revenue growth raised from over 30% to the mid-30s

quarterly_data.signal: Second wave data center customers: multiple new wins secured in Q1; Kelley said 'we've completed a number of qualifications in the first quarter, and we're working on additional ones this quarter' and those customers are now qualifying AE factories, 'typically a six to nine-month process'. Second wave customers expected to begin contributing meaningfully to revenue in 2027, with 'some potential to pull some of that revenue into the fourth quarter of 2026'. Oldham: they will not be the same size as the primary customers, 'but they could be meaningful, and there's several of them'.
quarterly_data.figure: factory qualification typically a six to nine-month process; meaningful revenue in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: 800 V transition: AE is sampling to key customers 800 V-50 V modules providing 4,000 W, 6,000 W and 8,000 W output power, differentiated by 'around 98% efficiency, high power density and high reliability'; Kelley: 'We've been told that we're leading from a technology standpoint.' Some small revenue this year, but 'it's starts in earnest in 2027 and becomes more meaningful in 2028'; the transition 'increases our dollar content per rack'.
quarterly_data.figure: 800 V-50 V modules at 4,000 W, 6,000 W and 8,000 W; around 98% efficiency; small revenue 2026, in earnest 2027, more meaningful 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity: expansion in Malaysia, the Philippines and Mexico in place in the second half of 2026, taking revenue-generating capacity to over $2.5 billion exiting the year. The new 500,000 sq ft Thailand facility is being brought up earlier than expected on data center and semiconductor strength (spending pulled from 2027 into 2H 2026); qualification builds for semiconductor and data center products start this quarter with initial production slated for late 2026 or early 2027; Thailand adds more than $1 billion of capacity for a total of over $3.5 billion. 2026 CapEx raised slightly on initial Thailand investment; Q1 CapEx was $37 million.
quarterly_data.figure: over $2.5 billion capacity exiting 2026; Thailand adds more than $1 billion, total over $3.5 billion; 2026 CapEx $170 million-$180 million

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance: Q2 revenue approximately $540 million, ±$20 million, with most sequential growth from semiconductor and industrial/medical; Q2 gross margin to improve 20 basis points-50 basis points sequentially; Q2 non-GAAP EPS $2.18, ±$0.25. Full-year 2026 revenue growth target raised from the high teens to the low-to-mid 20s, contemplating 'some tightening in supply and increasing input costs'. Oldham said gross margin 'could get to 41% by the end of the year'; long-term goal of over 43% (includes Thailand).
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue approximately $540 million, ±$20 million; EPS $2.18, ±$0.25; FY2026 growth low-to-mid 20s (from high teens); gross margin could reach 41% by year end

quarterly_data.signal: Supply: Kelley said the supply constraints so far have been downstream constraints at customers, and 'so far nothing has really stopped us from shipping product', while noting 'supply and cost challenges have begun to surface'. AE increased inventory, mostly in critical piece parts, to support growth and supply resiliency and to capture upside if customers clear their constraints; it developed more second sources after COVID and holds extra inventory where it could not. Inventory days rose to 135.
quarterly_data.figure: inventory increased by $48 million; inventory days 135

players.product: RF / DC plasma power supplies for etch & deposition tools

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor revenue grew 4% sequentially, finishing just below the mid-cycle peak of last year and flattish year-on-year; Kelley said customer forecasts 'strengthened considerably' in Q1, supporting record performance in 2026 and continued growth in 2027. Second-half 2026 semiconductor revenue expected to be up over 30% from the prior year, driven mainly by flagship (older, designed-in) products plus system power wins; Kelley: 'we are very happy with our backlog in semiconductor, and that's one of the reasons we're gonna be opening Thailand faster than we expected.'
quarterly_data.figure: semiconductor revenue $219 million (+4% sequentially); 2H 2026 semiconductor revenue up over 30% YoY

quarterly_data.signal: New plasma power products eVoS, eVerest and NavX: widespread customer acceptance at the leading edge in both memory and logic, with adoption spreading to other nodes and device types; Kelley: 'we're winning every battle that we're engaged in.' New products 'become significant starting in Q4 this year, but they become a bigger factor in 2027', with revenue meaningful into 2027 and 2028 as node transitions occur. On dielectric etch, Kelley expects to communicate wins later this year, tied to 'next generation nodes in DRAM and logic' rather than the NAND upgrade cycle.
quarterly_data.figure: new products significant starting Q4 2026, bigger factor in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Kelley: 'the constraint right now in semiconductor is really clean room space'; semiconductor customers are 'very enthusiastic about 2027' because 'there's a lot of new clean room space coming online in 2027'. He views AE shipments as more or less in sync with customer requirements, with increased orders driven primarily by the leading edge.

System power (the power the tool uses to operate, 'between the wall and the machine', distinct from plasma power injected into the chamber) is seeing an uptick in demand from recent wins in semiconductor testers and wafer fab equipment. IR's Edwin Mok restated that in aggregate plasma power is over a $1 billion market opportunity for AE.
quarterly_data.figure: plasma power over a $1 billion market opportunity
